title: Ordered Cech cup product
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U=(U_i)_{i\in I} any family of opens, and F,G O_X-modules, with tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and ordered Cech complexes [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]. The degree-(p,q) cup cochain is (a\cup b)_{i_0\ldots i_{p+q}}=a_{i_0\ldots i_p}|_{U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+q}}}\otimes b_{i_p\ldots i_{p+q}}|_{U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+q}}}. This is the specialization of the signed total tensor map of Tag 07MB to sheaves in degree zero (the component sign is +1). It obeys d(a\cup b)=da\cup b+(-1)^p a\cup db. Its induced cup product is the unique Gamma(X,O_X)-bilinear map check H^p(U,F)\times check H^q(U,G)\to check H^{p+q}(U,F\otimes G) carrying the classes of cocycles a,b to the class of their cup cochain. Classes use the kernel-to-homology construction shared with [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product]. No cover or finiteness condition is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07MB, cohomology-equation-needs-signs: degree-zero sheaf specialization and Leibniz

proof.text: Evaluate the categorical Cech differential through cechComplexFunctorIso and cechComplex_d_apply. Composition of restrictions identifies a twice restricted section with restriction along the composite face. Tensor restriction is compatible with tmulSection_map. These identities are proved by the private equiv_d, faceSection_comp, faceSection_d and faceSection_cup helpers.

At a fixed tuple, split the alternating sum over p+q+2 omitted vertices into the first p+1 and the last q+1 vertices using Fin.sum_univ_add. The first block is the front differential without its last term; the second is the back differential without its first term. The omitted last front term and first back term are the same tensor section with opposite signs. The private aw_sum proves this finite-sum identity, and equality of the face-index functions is proved with Fin.ext and omega. This proves cechCupCochain_leibniz.

Restriction maps are linear over global sections and tensor sections are bilinear. Through the cochain equivalences these give a bilinear cochain map cechCupLinear. The Leibniz formula shows that two cycles multiply to a cycle; restrict the pairing to the kernel modules to obtain cechCupCycles.

Products with boundaries are boundaries. In degree zero the incoming map is zero by the complex shape. In positive left degree p+1, Leibniz applied to a predecessor and a right cycle gives d(a cup b)=da cup b. In positive right degree q+1, apply Leibniz to a left cycle and a predecessor, then multiply by (-1)^p; the sign squares to one. Transport the target degree and use cycle_mem_range_of_d to exhibit the boundary preimages.

The cycle-class linear map is surjective, and its kernel is the range of the incoming differential, by moduleCatHomologyIso and Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero. Compose cechCupCycles with the target class map, use LinearMap.liftQ2 (Lean spelling liftQ₂) to descend through both boundary submodules, and transport along moduleCatHomologyIso. The private bilinear_homology_desc constructs this map and proves its value on cycle classes.

The constructed map satisfies IsCechCupProduct because a target cycle with the specified underlying section equals cechCupCycles of the two input cycles. Every class in each input homology module has a cycle representative; applying the prescribed cycle values to those representatives and linear-map extensionality proves uniqueness.
